text:
Marin: spun up nightglow-384 on staging — fp32 baseline and two quant variants: int8-per-channel and int6-per-channel asymmetric. ran short-query (5k) + topical cohort (5k) buckets.
Lee: nice. which index configs? faiss or hnsw?
Marin: ran both. summary paste: 
```
# faiss (IVF4096, PQ64, OPQ)
nightglow-384-fp32    r@1=0.624  r@5=0.801  p95=42.3ms
nightglow-384-int8pc  r@1=0.602  r@5=0.783  p95=24.8ms
nightglow-384-int6pc  r@1=0.583  r@5=0.768  p95=18.1ms
index: faiss IVF4096,PQ64,OPQ64
# hnsw (nmslib/hnsw) ef_search=128,M=32
nightglow-384-fp32    r@1=0.639  r@5=0.812  p95=36.5ms
nightglow-384-int8pc  r@1=0.619  r@5=0.796  p95=20.2ms
nightglow-384-int6pc  r@1=0.596  r@5=0.777  p95=15.0ms
```\nNoor: interesting — faiss PQ seems to penalize short queries more than hnsw. did you try OPQ+whitening before PQ?
Marin: yes OPQ enabled for faiss runs above. I also ran a control without OPQ: faiss w/o OPQ drops r@1 by ~0.01 for fp32 and ~0.03 for int6.
Lee: do we have stratified by token length?
Marin: short (<6) / med / long breakdown for hnsw: 
```
short: fp32=0.58 int8pc=0.50 int6pc=0.44
med:   fp32=0.64 int8pc=0.61 int6pc=0.58
long:  fp32=0.70 int8pc=0.69 int6pc=0.68
```\nNoor: int6 hit is concentrated on short alias/acronym queries. could be dynamic range clipping. what clamp/scale used?
Marin: quant configs: int8-per-channel symmetric, clamp=0.02; int6-per-channel asymmetric, outlier_clip=0.01, scale_sampling=topk1000, seed=2026.
ops-bot: reminder: include ef_search/IVF params in run name or tag — many runs missing ef tag.
Marin: noted. commands I ran:
```
python -m eval.run_embed_smoke --model nightglow-384 --quant none --index faiss --ivf 4096 --pq 64 --opq --out run_1788889990_fp32_faiss.json
python -m eval.run_embed_smoke --model nightglow-384 --quant int6-per-channel --index hnsw --ef_search 128 --out run_1788889990_int6_hnsw.json
```\nLee: next steps: 1) try per-channel int6 with stronger clamp (0.05) and re-evaluate short bucket, 2) run small A/B (5% short queries) routing to fp32 for 24h if int6-per-channel still >0.05 r@1 gap, 3) add top-10 failure pairs to Optimize regression set.
Noor: also try hybrid: use int6 for long queries and int8 for short queries via routing rule; likely keeps cost but protects alias recall.
Marin: will run clamp sweep (0.01/0.02/0.05) + hybrid routing sim later today. will upload UMAPs and failure pairs.
eval-bot: eval artifact uploaded -> https://internal/redwood/runs/1788889990 (contains per-cohort tables, UMAP before/after OPQ, failure pairs) :white_check_mark:
Marin: quick note — faiss PQ seems faster memory footprint but retrieval quality for short queries suffers unless OPQ+aggressive clamp present. documenting in onboarding draft.
Lee: great work. keep labels consistent. we'll sync tomorrow if clamp sweep doesn't close the short-query gap.
